pages.text: "Morning!" Kkiruk, the roof gull, tapped the round window. Dari pulled the quilt over his head. "A little longer... It's so cozy in here."
Dad came down after switching off the lighthouse lamp. "Sunrise! Time to gather shells." Dari shook his head beneath the quilt. "More sleep..." Then he snored again.
Much later, Dari woke with a start. The sun filled the window! He had promised to gather shells with Dad, but seawater already covered the shore rocks. "Already?" Dari pouted.
Dad sat beside the bed. "Getting up isn't hard. Stretch at sunrise." Holding Dari's front flippers, he helped him reach upward.
Front flippers long, tail flippers long—a whole-body stretch! Sleepiness slipped away and Dari felt fresh. "Stretching wakes me up! Sunrise, stretch!" He raised his nose toward the window.
Dad whispered, "Then open the window and greet the morning." Dari hopped down and pushed the round window open with a flipper.
Cool sea air drifted in, and waves splashed hello. Dari spread his flippers. "Hello, morning! Sunrise, stretch!" Kkiruk echoed from the roof.
Last, wash your face! Dari dipped into the bathroom basin's cool water and rubbed sleep from his eyes. Fresh and clean, he tapped his tail. "I started my morning myself!"
Now Dari knew the steps. "One, stretch at sunrise! Two, open the window and greet morning! Three, wash in cool water!" Next morning, he got up before Dad came down.
Dad hugged him. "Up bright as the morning sun! Let's gather shells today." A sunrise stretch chased sleep away. Sunrise, stretch!
